summary: The renders clearly depict a fixed-blade knife, but it is not yet convincing. Visually, the 286 mm blade is roughly 75 mm wide and the 118 mm grip roughly 54 mm wide, producing an oversized spear-point silhouette and a broad, short-looking handle that is implausible in a human hand. Narrow the grip to about 32–38 mm and lengthen its usable portion toward 125–135 mm; narrow the blade to roughly 40–50 mm with a clearer utilitarian drop/clip-point profile, and reduce the guard accordingly. The exposed pommel ring also looks snag-prone; integrate the lanyard hole into the tang or make the loop sturdier and less prominent. Most decisively, both actual-GLB renders are nearly uniform pale grey: rubber, oxide, blade steel, bevel, and pins have no useful material separation. Fix the exported material/color pipeline and validate under neutral lighting so the grip reads dark and matte, the fittings blackened, and the blade metallic with a restrained brighter bevel. The 0.4425 m overall length correctly treats catalogue reach 1.3 m as gameplay reach, while 584 triangles and four materials suit the Halo CE-era budget. The named root and grip/blade/tip markers are useful. Rewrite the README before rebuilding: remove the false claim that this export’s material separation was visibly validated and the assertion that the current geometry is already credible; document narrower hand-scale targets, then record actual post-export visual findings. metrics.json’s passed flag should be described as technical validation, not visual approval.
